description:
## Goal Build the Inventory holds example in examples/inventory/. This example validates use_hold/3, the Filament.Hold.GenServer macro, and the automatic hold-release on process death (:DOWN). The core claim: closing the tab (killing the fiber process) immediately restores available inventory — no TTL, no cleanup job. Component: CheckoutLineItem calls use_hold(Inventory.Server, item_id) and renders either a "Checkout" button (hold acquired) or an "Out of Stock" message (hold returned {:error, :insufficient}). Validates: use_hold, Hold.GenServer, handle_acquire, handle_release, :DOWN lifecycle, error path rendering. ## Deviation policy Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run `bw comment "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await guidance. Do not improvise. --- ## 0. Prerequisites Read Track E (flm-zoc) implementation before writing: - lib/filament/hold.ex — Filament.Hold behaviour callbacks - lib/filament/hold/gen_server.ex — the `use Filament.Hold.GenServer` macro - lib/filament/hooks.ex — use_hold/3 signature and return values Confirm: - What does use_hold/3 return? {:held, server, token} | {:error, reason} | :uninitialized? - What does handle_acquire/3 receive? (request, holder_pid, state)? - What does handle_acquire/3 return on success? {:ok, token, new_state}? - What does handle_acquire/3 return on failure? {:error, reason, state}? - Does handle_release/3 receive the token? Or just the holder_pid? - Is handle_release/3 optional (default no-op)? Also add "examples/inventory/lib" to elixirc_paths(:test) in filament/mix.exs (following the pattern from G1 and G2). --- ## 1. Add examples/inventory/lib to elixirc_paths FILE: filament/mix.exs (update elixirc_paths(:test)) ```elixir defp elixirc_paths(:test) do [ "lib", "test/support", "examples/todo/lib", "examples/cart/lib", "examples/inventory/lib" # add this line ] end ``` --- ## 2. examples/inventory/mix.exs Same structure as examples/todo/mix.exs. App name :inventory. Module Inventory.MixProject. --- ## 3. Domain — Inventory.Item struct FILE: examples/inventory/lib/inventory/item.ex ```elixir defmodule Inventory.Item do @enforce_keys [:id, :name] defstruct [:id, :name, available: 1] @type t :: %__MODULE__{ id: String.t(), name: String.t(), available: non_neg_integer() } end ``` --- ## 4. Domain — Inventory.Server (Hold GenServer) FILE: examples/inventory/lib/inventory/server.ex Inventory.Server tracks available stock per item. Each call to handle_acquire/3 decrements the available count and stores the hold. handle_release/3 restores the count. The :DOWN handler in Hold.GenServer (injected by the macro) calls handle_release/3 when the holder process dies. ```elixir defmodule Inventory.Server do use Filament.Hold.GenServer # State: %{item_id => %Inventory.Item{}} @type state :: %{String.t() => Inventory.Item.t()} def start_link(opts \\ []) do initial_items = Keyword.get(opts, :items, []) name = Keyword.get(opts, :name, __MODULE__) GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, initial_items, name: name) end def get_item(server \\ __MODULE__, item_id) do GenServer.call(server, {:get_item, item_id}) end # GenServer callbacks @impl GenServer def init(items) do state = Map.new(items, fn item -> {item.id, item} end) {:ok, state} end # Hold callbacks — called by the Hold.GenServer macro on acquire/release. # request is the item_id passed to use_hold/3. # holder_pid is the subscribing fiber's pid. @impl Filament.Hold def handle_acquire(item_id, _holder_pid, state) do case Map.get(state, item_id) do nil -> {:error, :not_found, state} %{available: 0} -> {:error, :insufficient, state} item -> token = {item_id, make_ref()} new_item = %{item | available: item.available - 1} {:ok, token, Map.put(state, item_id, new_item)} end end # handle_release/3 is called when the holder process dies (:DOWN) or explicitly # releases the hold. The token was returned by handle_acquire/3. # Check Track E for the exact signature — it may be (token, holder_pid, state) # or (request, token, state) or another shape. Adjust if needed. @impl Filament.Hold def handle_release({item_id, _ref}, _holder_pid, state) do case Map.get(state, item_id) do nil -> {:ok, state} item -> new_item = %{item | available: item.available + 1} {:ok, Map.put(state, item_id, new_item)} end end @impl GenServer def handle_call({:get_item, item_id}, _from, state) do {:reply, Map.get(state, item_id), state} end end ``` CRITICAL NOTE on handle_release/3 signature: Track E's spec says handle_release receives (request, holder_pid, state) where request is what was passed to use_hold/3 (i.e., item_id). But we also need the token to do cleanup. Check Track E's Filament.Hold behaviour definition (lib/filament/hold.ex) for the exact callback signature. The token may be accessible via the process dictionary entry stored by Hold.GenServer. Adjust the signature above to match. --- ## 5. UI — CheckoutLineItem component FILE: examples/inventory/lib/inventory_web/components/checkout_line_item.ex CheckoutLineItem mounts with a hold on the requested item. If the hold succeeds, it renders a checkout button. If {:error, :insufficient}, it renders out-of-stock. ```elixir defmodule InventoryWeb.Components.CheckoutLineItem do use Filament.Component prop :item_id, :string, required: true prop :server, :any, default: Inventory.Server def render(assigns) do # use_hold/3 returns: # {:held, server, token} — hold acquired successfully # {:error, :insufficient} — no stock available # {:error, :not_found} — unknown item_id # :uninitialized — before first acquire attempt # Check Track E (flm-zoc.1) for exact return shape. hold_result = use_hold(assigns.server, assigns.item_id) item = Inventory.Server.get_item(assigns.server, assigns.item_id) ~F"""
<%= case hold_result do %> <% {:held, _server, _token} -> %> <%= item && item.name %> <% {:error, :insufficient} -> %> <%= item && item.name %> Out of Stock <% {:error, :not_found} -> %> Item not found: <%= @item_id %> <% :uninitialized -> %> Checking availability… <% end %>
""" end end ``` NOTE: The `case hold_result do` inside a ~F template may require a different syntax depending on Track B's template implementation. If ~F uses EEx under the hood, the `<% case ... do %>` syntax may need adjusting. Check how conditional rendering is done in Track B's ~F templates and adjust accordingly. --- ## 6. UI — Inventory LiveView host FILE: examples/inventory/lib/inventory_web/live/inventory_live.ex Demonstrates multiple CheckoutLineItem components sharing one Inventory.Server. Each CheckoutLineItem independently holds its item slot. ```elixir defmodule InventoryWeb.InventoryLive do use Phoenix.LiveView use Filament.LiveView @impl true def mount(_params, _session, socket) do items = [ %Inventory.Item{id: "item-1", name: "Blue Widget", available: 2}, %Inventory.Item{id: "item-2", name: "Red Gadget", available: 1}, %Inventory.Item{id: "item-3", name: "Green Doohickey", available: 0} ] {:ok, server} = Inventory.Server.start_link(items: items) {:ok, assign(socket, server: server, item_ids: Enum.map(items, & &1.id))} end @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""

Inventory Demo

<%= for item_id <- @item_ids do %> <%= Filament.mount_component( InventoryWeb.Components.CheckoutLineItem, item_id: item_id, server: @server ) %> <% end %>
""" end end ``` --- ## 7. Test: verify hold acquire/release lifecycle FILE: test/filament/examples/inventory_test.exs ```elixir defmodule Filament.Examples.InventoryTest do use ExUnit.Case, async: true alias Inventory.{Item, Server} defp start_server(items) do {:ok, server} = Server.start_link(items: items) server end test "acquire hold decrements available" do item = %Item{id: "x", name: "X", available: 2} server = start_server([item]) # Acquire via Filament.Hold.acquire/3 (Track E public API). # Check lib/filament/hold.ex for the exact function name. assert {:ok, _token} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "x", self()) after_first = Server.get_item(server, "x") assert after_first.available == 1 end test "acquire returns {:error, :insufficient} when none available" do item = %Item{id: "y", name: "Y", available: 1} server = start_server([item]) assert {:ok, _token} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "y", self()) assert {:error, :insufficient} = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "y", self()) end test "process death releases hold and restores availability" do item = %Item{id: "z", name: "Z", available: 1} server = start_server([item]) # Acquire from a spawned process so we can kill it. parent = self() holder = spawn(fn -> result = Filament.Hold.acquire(server, "z", self()) send(parent, {:acquired, result}) receive do: (:die -> :ok) end) assert_receive {:acquired, {:ok, _token}}, 500 # Verify hold is active — available should be 0. assert Server.get_item(server, "z").available == 0 # Kill the holder — :DOWN should trigger handle_release. Process.exit(holder, :kill) Process.sleep(50) # give the monitor time to fire # Available should be restored. assert Server.get_item(server, "z").available == 1 end test "CheckoutLineItem module exists" do assert Code.ensure_loaded?(InventoryWeb.Components.CheckoutLineItem) end end ``` NOTE: `Filament.Hold.acquire/3` may not be a public function — Track E's use_hold/3 is the hook-based API. Check whether Track E provides a lower-level acquire function for testing, or whether you need to test hold behavior differently. If Filament.Hold.acquire/3 does not exist, adapt the test to use use_hold/3 via Filament.Test (from Track F). In that case, mark this test @tag :pending and document the dependency. --- ## Completion criteria 1. `mix compile` succeeds from `examples/inventory/` (standalone). 2. `mix compile` succeeds from `filament/` with updated elixirc_paths. 3. `mix test test/filament/examples/inventory_test.exs` passes all 4 tests (or passes the non-pending tests, with any pending tests noted and explained). 4. No compiler warnings.
title: G3: Inventory holds example — use_hold, process-death release, out-of-stock UX
